title: Cohomology of scalar reduction and signed single-sheaf identifications
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a final object [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $n\geq1$, and put $Z=\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ and $R=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their cohomological unbounded derived categories and shift convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $Lq=-\otimes_Z^L R:D(Z)\to D(R)$ be derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], let $\operatorname{Res}:D(R)\to D(Z)$ be termwise restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and let $\eta$ be the unit of the adjunction induced by ordinary scalar extension and restriction [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. For an abelian sheaf $A$, use a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to A[0]$ and write $Q_A=P/nP$ for its $R$-complex representing $Lq(A)$; let $\delta_A:\operatorname{Res}Lq(A)\to A[1]$ be the last map of the multiplication triangle [lem-sfb-scalar-reduction-unit-triangle]. Its cohomology is zero outside degrees $-1,0$, and there is an exact sequence of abelian sheaves
$$0\to H^{-1}(\operatorname{Res}Lq(A))\xrightarrow{H^{-1}(\delta_A)}A\xrightarrow{n}A\xrightarrow{H^0(\eta_A)}H^0(\operatorname{Res}Lq(A))\to0.$$
For every complex $Q$ of $R$-modules with cohomology only in degree $a\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical truncation zigzag $Q\leftarrow\tau_{\leq a}Q\to H^a(Q)[-a]$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] is a natural pair of $R$-linear quasi-isomorphisms. In particular, for an abelian sheaf $F$ such that $n:F\to F$ is monic, with $\bar F=\operatorname{coker}(n:F\to F)$ and quotient $p_F:F\to\bar F$, there is an isomorphism $\alpha_F:Lq(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar F[0]$ satisfying $(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_F)\eta_F=p_F$.
For an abelian sheaf $B$ such that $n:B\to B$ is epic, put $H=\ker(n:B\to B)$, let $i:H\hookrightarrow B$, and let $\kappa_B:B\to H[1]$ be the boundary of $0\to H\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{n}B\to0$ [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]. There is an isomorphism $\alpha_B:Lq(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}H[1]$ in $D(R)$ such that
$$(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_B)\eta_B=\kappa_B,\qquad (-i[1])\operatorname{Res}(\alpha_B)=\delta_B.$$
Its map on degree $-1$ cohomology is the uniquely determined isomorphism $v:H^{-1}(\operatorname{Res}Lq(B))\to H$ with $(-i)v=H^{-1}(\delta_B)$. Every additive map between abelian sheaves killed by $n$ is $R$-linear [lem-pur-torsion-sheaf-constant-module], so the cohomology identifications and the displayed isomorphisms hold in $D(R)$, with the sign given by the rotated triangle $B\xrightarrow{n}B\xrightarrow{\kappa_B}H[1]\xrightarrow{-i[1]}B[1]$.

proof.text: Put $K_A=\operatorname{Res}Lq(A)$. The scalar-reduction triangle gives $A\xrightarrow{n}A\xrightarrow{\eta_A}K_A\xrightarrow{\delta_A}A[1]$ with precisely the specified unit and last map. Apply the long exact cohomology sequence of a distinguished triangle to this triangle and to its rotations $A\xrightarrow{\eta_A}K_A\xrightarrow{\delta_A}A[1]\xrightarrow{-n[1]}A[1]$ and $K_A\xrightarrow{\delta_A}A[1]\xrightarrow{-n[1]}A[1]\xrightarrow{-\eta_A[1]}K_A[1]$, which are distinguished by TR2. Exactness at the middle term of each triangle is exactness of $H^j$ applied to its first two maps, so the sequence below consists of the cohomology maps of $\eta_A$, $\delta_A$ and $\pm n$, not of unspecified connecting morphisms; the sign of $-n$ does not change kernels or images. Since $A[0]$ has cohomology $A$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere, the terms in each degree outside $-1,0$ force $H^j(K_A)=0$. The remaining segment is $0\to H^{-1}(K_A)\xrightarrow{H^{-1}(\delta_A)}A\xrightarrow{n}A\xrightarrow{H^0(\eta_A)}H^0(K_A)\to0$, using $H^{-1}(A[1])=A$. This is the asserted exact sequence, with its actual maps, rather than just an identification of its objects.

proof.text: Restriction is exact by the ordinary ringed-site scalar-adjunction theorem, applied to $Z\to R$. In particular it preserves kernels, images and cokernels, so termwise restriction gives $\operatorname{Res}H^a(Q)=H^a(\operatorname{Res}Q)$, including the induced maps. It is conservative on sheaves: a map with an invertible underlying additive map has an $R$-linear inverse, since $f(rx)=rf(x)$ implies $f^{-1}(ry)=rf^{-1}(y)$. Thus vanishing computed in Step 1 also holds for the $R$-cohomology of $Q_A$. Exact termwise restriction induces the triangulated functor on derived categories, commutes with shifts and single complexes, and sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. These are the comparisons used below.

source.place: Tags 03D7 and 03DA, scalar restriction; termwise derived exactness from the cited exact-functor node

proof.text: For a complex $Q$ with cohomology only in degree $a$, set $T=\tau_{\le a}Q$. Its terms are $Q^j$ for $j<a$, $\ker d_Q^a$ for $j=a$, and zero for $j>a$. Let $c:T\to Q$ be the inclusion and let $p:T\to H^a(Q)[-a]$ have sole nonzero component the quotient $\ker d_Q^a\to\ker d_Q^a/\operatorname{im}d_Q^{a-1}$ in degree $a$. The equation $p^a d_T^{a-1}=0$ makes $p$ a chain map. Directly from these kernels and quotients, $H^j(c)$ is the identity for $j\le a$, while $H^a(p)$ is the identity and both sides have zero cohomology in every other degree. Hence $c,p$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Their components are $R$-linear; a chain map preserves cycles and boundaries, so it commutes with both $c$ and $p$. This proves the natural $R$-linear zigzag and defines $\epsilon_Q=Q(p)Q(c)^{-1}$, inducing the identity on $H^a$. The same formulas apply to abelian sheaves. Restriction carries these maps to the identical kernel/quotient maps under Step 2's comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, canonical cochain truncations; explicit cycles-to-cohomology quotient

proof.text: We will use the following immediate consequence of the preceding zigzag and full faithfulness of the single-complex embedding. If $X,Y$ have cohomology only in the same degree $a$, conjugating a morphism $u:X\to Y$ by $\epsilon_X,\epsilon_Y$ and shifting by $a$ identifies it with a unique ordinary map $H^a(X)\to H^a(Y)$. Applying $H^a$ shows that this map is $H^a(u)$, since both $\epsilon$ maps induce identities. Thus two such morphisms are equal if their $H^a$ maps agree, and every isomorphism of these cohomology objects gives an isomorphism $X\to Y$. This also shows that the isomorphisms from Step 3 are natural for derived morphisms, not merely for chain maps. We use the assertion separately in the abelian categories of $Z$-sheaves and of $R$-sheaves, never full faithfulness of derived restriction.

source.place: Tag 06XS, lemma-negative-exts (2), together with Step 3 and the shift autoequivalence

proof.text: Suppose $n:F\to F$ is monic. Step 1 gives $H^{-1}(K_F)=0$, and $h=H^0(\eta_F):F\to H^0(K_F)$ is a cokernel of $n$. The cokernel universal property supplies the unique isomorphism $t:H^0(K_F)\to\bar F$ with $th=p_F$. Both sheaves are killed by $n$: for $\bar F$ this follows from $p_Fn=0$, and for $H^0(K_F)$ it follows from its $R$-module structure. The torsion-sheaf module theorem makes $t$ $R$-linear. Form $\alpha_F=t[0]\epsilon_{Q_F}c_F$ in $D(R)$, where $c_F:Lq(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_F$ is the given resolution comparison. Its restriction composed with $\eta_F$ induces $th=p_F$ on $H^0$. Both this composite and $p_F$ are morphisms from $F[0]$ to $\bar F[0]$, so Step 4 proves equality. This proves the monic case including its unit normalization.

source.place: Tags 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, and 06XS, lemma-negative-exts; cokernel comparison and Steps 1–4

proof.text: Suppose $n:B\to B$ is epic. The short exact sequence $0\to H\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{n}B\to0$ gives the distinguished triangle $H\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{n}B\xrightarrow{\kappa_B}H[1]$. By signed rotation its rotation is $B\xrightarrow{n}B\xrightarrow{\kappa_B}H[1]\xrightarrow{-i[1]}B[1]$. Compare this with $B\xrightarrow{n}B\xrightarrow{\eta_B}K_B\xrightarrow{\delta_B}B[1]$. TR3 applied to the identity on each of the first two copies of $B$ gives $u:K_B\to H[1]$ satisfying $u\eta_B=\kappa_B$ and $(-i[1])u=\delta_B$. Taking $H^{-1}$ yields $(-i)H^{-1}(u)=H^{-1}(\delta_B)$. By Step 1 the map on the right identifies its source with $\ker n$, and $-i:H\to B$ is also a kernel of $n$. Consequently $v=H^{-1}(u)$ is the unique isomorphism with $(-i)v=H^{-1}(\delta_B)$. Notice that the rotation forces the minus sign.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor; Tag 0145, definition-triangulated-category, TR2 and TR3

proof.text: Step 1 and epicness give $H^0(K_B)=0$; thus $K_B$ and $Q_B$ are concentrated in cohomological degree $-1$. Also $nH=0$ since $ni=0$ and $i$ is monic. The torsion-sheaf module theorem makes $v:H^{-1}(K_B)\to H$ $R$-linear. In $D(R)$ define $\alpha_B=v[1]\epsilon_{Q_B}c_B:Lq(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}H[1]$, using the cohomology comparison of Step 2. Its restriction and the map $u$ from Step 6 have the same map $v$ on $H^{-1}$. Step 4 in $D(Z)$ therefore gives $\operatorname{Res}(\alpha_B)=u$. Substituting in the two equations from TR3 proves $(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_B)\eta_B=\kappa_B$ and $(-i[1])\operatorname{Res}(\alpha_B)=\delta_B$. It also proves the stated uniqueness characterization of the degree $-1$ map. All isomorphisms were constructed by $R$-linear maps and the $R$-linear truncation zigzag; only their comparison with the two $Z$-linear boundaries was made after restriction.
